beats.narration_text: Hi, I'm Sai Pranavi J. This video is about a button labeled 'Select All,' sitting right at the top of a feed list, that could silently break every question you asked afterward, and an error message that never once told you why.
beats.new_visual_element: Personal-intro card: name + one-line plain-language summary, spoken

shot.note: Same pattern as this fellow's other episodes' B01.

beats.narration_text: Our chat assistant has a hard limit: ten feeds per question, a deliberate cap on how much context goes to the model. The feed panel loads up to a hundred items. And the single most obvious thing to click, 'Select All,' had no limit at all.
beats.new_visual_element: Two tiles side by side: the backend's real 10-feed cap, versus Select All's real pre-fix code with no cap, visually flagged as a mismatch

shot.note: Real framing of the unguarded, most-discoverable UI action, not illustrative.

beats.narration_text: Here's the real code. Select All used to set every loaded feed selected, no limit, no check. The backend's own feed query caps feed ids at ten items, by design, so the model's context doesn't blow up. And when that cap got violated, the chat's error handler only ever showed axios's own generic message: request failed with status code four twenty two. The real reason FastAPI sent back was sitting right there in the response. The code just never read it.
beats.new_visual_element: The real pre-fix handleSelectAll/handleToggle, the real backend max_items=10 field, and the real pre-fix generic error line, shown verbatim

shot.note: [Source: Regulatory_QA/frontend/src/App.jsx, src/components/ChatInterface.jsx (pre-fix); E1-VERIFICATION.md] Verbatim pre-fix code, not paraphrased.

beats.narration_text: The fix caps selection at ten, in both places: the button, and clicking feeds one at a time, because eleven individual clicks would hit the exact same outage. And the chat's error handler now reads the server's real reason first, falling back to the generic message only when there isn't one.
beats.new_visual_element: The real diff: MAX_SELECTABLE_FEEDS = 10 added and both selection paths capped in App.jsx; the real detail-extraction block added to ChatInterface.jsx's catch clause

shot.note: [Source: E1-VERIFICATION.md, 'The fix'] Real diff, matches the committed fix exactly.

beats.narration_text: I extracted both fixes into a live Node harness and ran five checks. Select All against a four hundred eleven feed table now selects exactly ten. Fifteen individual clicks in a row stop adding at ten. Untoggling one and adding another still holds the cap. And the error message that used to read 'request failed with status code four twenty two' now reads the real reason: list should have at most ten items after validation, not fifteen. All seven assertions across those five checks pass.
beats.new_visual_element: The real before/after table from this session's own harness run: 5 checks, old vs. new behavior, the real captured 422 message text

shot.note: [Source: verification/verify_feed_cap_output.txt; E1-VERIFICATION.md] Real measured harness results from this session, matching E1-VERIFICATION.md's own table exactly.

beats.narration_text: Two honest limits. First: this was verified against the extracted logic in a Node harness, not a running browser build. Node modules isn't installed here, so there was no full vite build or end-to-end browser check, only the I-D-E's own static diagnostics, which came back with zero new errors. Second: nothing was added to actually tell the user selection stopped growing at ten. No disabled state, no tooltip. It just silently stops. That's a reasonable follow-up, not done yet.
beats.new_visual_element: 2 honest-limit cards, side by side, full weight: no vite build/browser check done, and no UI cap indicator added

shot.note: [Source: E1-VERIFICATION.md 'Verification'/'What's NOT touched'; RUN_LOG.md 2026-11-12 'Open issues'] Full weight, not softened.

beats.narration_text: The most obvious button in the interface is exactly the one that needs to respect the system's real limits. And when something does fail, showing the real reason is what turns an outage into something a user can actually fix.
